steps.title: A smaller triad
steps.body:
**diminished triad** means a root with a note three half steps above it and another six half steps above it. B, D and F make B diminished, written Bdim or B°.

**Why it matters:** The chord built on the seventh note of a major scale has this smaller shape.

steps.title: See it on the fretboard
steps.body: For a compact example, use B2 at string 5 fret 2, F3 at string 4 fret 3, B3 at string 3 fret 4 and D4 at string 2 fret 3. The repeated B is still the root. The app checks sounds, not a required hand shape.

items.prompt: Play B, D and F together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Explore the sounds
steps.body: Compare B, D, F with B, D, F#. Only the last sound changes; the diminished version is one half step smaller.
